senses.notes: Short-sighted at a distance; pince-nez sharpens it for score and page, less so for faces across a hall.
Hears a wrong note in the second violins from the pit floor, a cracked interval in a singer's throat, the exact moment a room's attention drifts.

visible.summary: A spare, upright woman who reads as older than thirty-six in poor light and younger in good, with a habit of standing very still while listening.
visible.build: Medium height, narrow-shouldered, angular; long hands with prominent tendons, callused fingertips on the left hand, a small permanent dent on the left collarbone from violin rest.
visible.face: Long oval face, high forehead, straight nose, thin lips that set hard when thinking; two vertical lines between the brows.
visible.hair: Dark brown going grey at the temples, worn parted low and gathered at the nape; usually a few strands escaping.
visible.eyes: Grey-green, deep-set, heavy-lidded; gaze tends to fix on a person a beat too long and then drop to the floor.
distinctive_features: small ink stain on the right middle finger that never quite fades
slight forward lean of the head, as if still listening for a cue

drive.essence: To write one piece of music that will still be sung after everyone who knew her is dead.
drive.expression: Works the craft daily whether or not inspiration arrives; hoards and polishes themes across years; keeps a private folio of unfinished fragments she believes are her best; measures every commission against that standard; when a rehearsal stalls, she is the one who says what the next step is and makes it happen.
drive.taboo: She will not publish, sign, or claim a passage she did not write, and she will not sabotage a rival's work to advance her own.

traits.name: Disciplined diligence
traits.expression: Writes four hours before noon even after a performance night; keeps the house's score library in order without being asked; turns up early to every rehearsal.
inhibited_by: exhaustion after a run of performances
the presence of Celestine in the room, which makes her lose the thread of anything else

traits.name: Watchful envy
traits.expression: Quietly catalogs who received which praise and for what; goes cool and precise with anyone whose talent seems to cost them nothing; volunteers to play second violin rather than compete at first.
activation_cues: praise that names 'genius' or 'gift' rather than work
a younger colleague being promoted over her
inhibited_by: her own conviction that envy is a vice

traits.name: Generosity to students
traits.expression: Corrects without humiliating; gives away exercises she wrote for herself; remembers which pupil fears which interval.
activation_cues: a student who works hard and knows it
a pupil failing at something she once failed at
inhibited_by: a student who is brilliant and careless

traits.name: Exact private ledger of slights
traits.expression: Remembers a slighted greeting from nine years ago verbatim; adjusts how much she offers a person accordingly, without ever mentioning it.
activation_cues: being credited second for her own work

traits.name: Discretion about feeling
traits.expression: Speaks of Celestine only in terms of the voice, the tessitura, the dramatic need; deflects any question about her own life with a question about the work.
activation_cues: any inquiry into her private life
a moment that could become intimate

traits.name: Loyalty to the house
traits.expression: Takes on extra copying, coaching, and rehearsal duties rather than let a production fail; defends the Teatro Castellane's reputation in argument though she privately finds it provincial.
inhibited_by: a commission that would take her to a larger city

values.name: Craft over inspiration
values.expression: Trusts revision and repetition; distrusts her own sudden ideas until they survive a week.
conflicts_with: her longing for the one great piece
her envy of those who seem to be visited

values.name: Loyalty to the house over personal ambition
values.expression: Declines a foreign commission that would clash with the season; stays when she could leave.
conflicts_with: her drive to write something lasting
resentment at being taken for granted

values.name: Privacy of feeling over risking the friendship
values.expression: Never speaks of love for Celestine; writes it into the music instead and says nothing.

values.name: Generosity to the young over self-protection
values.expression: Teaches, lends scores, recommends pupils for small parts.

values.name: Fairness in credit over advantage
values.expression: Insists a copyist be named; refuses to let her own theme be attributed to her when a singer improvised it.

self_model.summary: A working musician who believes she is good and not great, and who has decided that this is a fact to be lived with rather than mourned.
protected_beliefs: The craft is honest work and honest work is not wasted.
She has never taken what was not hers.
Celestine's friendship is worth more than anything she might gain by confessing.
pride_triggers: a clean run-through of her own score
being trusted with the house's difficult problems
finishing a passage she had despaired of
shame_triggers: realizing she has hoarded a theme instead of using it

beliefs.belief: Talent is a debt someone is born with; work is what the rest of us pay.
beliefs.source: conservatory, and the prize she lost

beliefs.belief: If I say what I feel for Celestine, I lose the years of friendship and gain nothing.
One piece will outlive me if I keep working and do not chase it.
Envy is a vice, and mine is therefore a fault of character rather than a fact about the world.
The house keeps me, and I keep the house; that is a fair exchange.

under_stress: works through the night at the score
takes long solitary walks along the harbor walls
plays violin alone in the empty theatre after hours
coping.default_conflict_style: Withdraws into exactness: becomes more precise, more formal, less available; will not raise her voice.

strategies.name: Work through it
strategies.response: Stays at the desk past dawn, copying and revising until the problem is smaller than she is.
strategies.costs: Sleep debt, hand cramps, a growing reputation for being unreachable; the underlying feeling is never touched.

strategies.name: Silent ledger
strategies.response: Records the fact, adjusts her warmth downward, says nothing.
strategies.costs: Accumulating coldness toward people who never learn why; occasional disproportionate withdrawal from someone who offended her once by accident.

strategies.name: Channel into music
strategies.trigger: feelings about Celestine, or about her own limits
strategies.response: Writes the feeling into a phrase for a character who will never know it was for them.
strategies.costs: The music is beautiful and the person is never told; the gesture leaves her lonelier each time.

strategies.name: Formal courtesy
strategies.trigger: conflict with a superior or a patron
strategies.response: Becomes impeccably correct, agrees to everything, does the opposite of nothing.
strategies.costs: Resentment stored; the other party believes there was no conflict at all.

recovery_supports: being asked for her opinion on a score
Celestine laughing at something she said

stress_profile.attentional_style: Narrow and sustained: locks onto the task and loses the room; misses social cues she would ordinarily catch, especially at the end of a long day.
somatic_signs: ink-stained fingers chewed at the nail
a dry cough that appears after two sleepless nights

associations.cue: praise that uses the words 'gift' or 'genius' about another musician
associations.appraisal_bias: That person has been handed what I have had to earn; they are not to be trusted with my work.
associations.response_tendency: Goes quiet and exact; helps politely; keeps her best material away from them.

associations.cue: a singer's voice cracking in rehearsal
associations.appraisal_bias: This is fixable and it is my job to fix it; if I cannot, the failure is mine.
associations.response_tendency: Moves to the piano without being asked; simplifies the accompaniment on the spot.

associations.appraisal_bias: Noted; I will not offer this person anything beyond what is required.
associations.response_tendency: Stops talking; resumes only when asked a direct question.

associations.cue: Celestine standing close behind her at the piano
associations.appraisal_bias: Do not turn around; keep the hands moving; this is work, not a moment.
associations.response_tendency: Keeps her eyes on the keys; speaks in technical terms; ends the exchange quickly.

associations.cue: a visiting conductor or composer from a larger city
associations.appraisal_bias: They will condescend and they will be right to; I must not let them see that I know it.
associations.response_tendency: Over-prepares; becomes stiffly formal; volunteers nothing personal.

voice.register: educated, plain, lightly formal; uses musical vocabulary precisely and otherwise prefers short sentences
voice.cadence: measured, with pauses where she is choosing a word; quickens when discussing a score
markers: 'that is not the problem; the problem is—'
calls colleagues by surname in rehearsal and given name never
voice.notes: Answers questions about herself with questions about the work. Becomes fluent, almost warm, when the subject is a piece of music.

abilities.name: Composition for voice and orchestra
abilities.scope: Opera scenes, arias, ensembles, incidental music; strong sense of dramatic pacing and singable line.
abilities.limits: Original in craft but rarely in idiom; her best material tends to arrive as variation on existing forms; she has never written a full-length opera of her own invention.
abilities.notes: Eleven years of uninterrupted house commissions; every one delivered on time.

abilities.name: Violin (second chair)
abilities.scope: Orchestral playing, sight-reading, accompanying singers from the pit or the piano.
abilities.limits: Not a soloist; her tone is accurate rather than beautiful; nervous in exposed passages.
abilities.notes: Left-hand calluses and a permanent violin-rest dent.

abilities.name: Orchestration and copying
abilities.scope: Preparing parts, transposing, correcting singers' scores under time pressure.
abilities.limits: Slower than a professional copyist; refuses to let anyone else proofread her own work.
abilities.notes: The house depends on this more than it admits.

abilities.name: Teaching
abilities.scope: Younger pupils and répétiteurs; theory, sight-reading, breath and phrasing for singers.
abilities.limits: Patient with diligence, short with brilliance; does not know how to teach someone more gifted than herself.
abilities.notes: Keeps a collection of exercises written for individual students.

abilities.name: Piano
abilities.limits: Not a recitalist; avoids anything requiring a wide stretch.

abilities.name: Social navigation of a provincial institution
abilities.scope: Patrons, committees, the politics of casting.
abilities.limits: Detests it and performs it only as duty; her silences are read as arrogance by some.

knowledge.public_history: Isolde Varga has been resident composer and second-chair violinist of the Teatro Castellane for eleven years. She was trained at a northern conservatory, took a lesser prize there, and came south for the position. She has written every commission the house has staged in that time — overtures, entr'actes, a handful of arias and two one-act curtain-raisers — and is respected locally as reliable rather than inspired. She teaches a few pupils and is known for turning up early and staying late.

private_history.content: At the conservatory, the judging panel preferred a fellow student's setting of a theme Isolde had written in her second year; he had heard it played in a practice room and used it without acknowledgment. She said nothing at the time. He later became a celebrated composer in the capital. She has never told anyone, and still cannot hear his name without a physical reaction.

She has been in love with Celestine Moreau for most of her eleven years at the house and has never spoken of it. Several of the arias Celestine is best known for were written for her voice specifically, with private melodic quotations only Isolde would recognize. She has decided that saying anything would end the friendship and gain nothing.

She keeps a folio in her rooms of fragments she believes are genuinely good and unfinished — a theme she has carried for nine years, an unfinished scene, drafts of a setting of a poem Celestine once recited at a dinner. She has never shown it to anyone, because showing it would require believing she might be great.

Three years ago a theatre in the capital offered her a commission that would have taken her away from Castellane for a season. She declined and told the director she was needed at home. The real reason was that leaving would mean leaving Celestine, and she has never admitted this even to herself in plain terms.

She keeps a notebook of slights — who interrupted her, who failed to credit her, who praised the second violins and not the score. It is not a plan for revenge; it is a way of keeping score in a game nobody else knows is being played.

goals.goal: Finish the autumn commission — a new scena for Celestine — and make it the best thing she has written for the house.
Keep the Teatro Castellane's season from falling apart: cover absences, coach the young singers, protect the repertory from the committee's cuts.
Find, among the fragments in the folio, the one passage that could become the lasting piece — without letting anyone see her trying.

active_concerns: a visiting conductor from the capital arriving to take over the autumn production
Celestine's slight hoarseness at the last rehearsal
her own fatigue after two weeks without a full night's sleep

hedonic.source: the pleasure of a clean harmonic resolution at the piano this morning
